clue.text: Key to enter dwelling always reversed, note

indicators.note: to enter means the key goes into the middle of the dwelling and the reversed word

parts.note: a semi is a semi-detached house, a dwelling

indicators.note: reversed means the word for always is read backwards

parts.note: always means ever
B is a musical key

explanation.surface: Someone always backs the key into the door of their home, with a note.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Key' reads as something for a lock, but it is the musical key B; the reversed word sits after the house, and B slips between them.
explanation.definitionFit: A semibreve is a whole note in music, the longest note value in common use.

clue.text: Part with ease? Possibly

indicators.note: possibly means the letters of part and ease could be arranged otherwise

explanation.surface: A question of whether a parting can be done easily.
explanation.definitionFit: To divide or split up is to separate, and the clue's letters rearranged do it.

clue.text: Queen's speech?

parts.note: a queen is also a female cat, whose speech is its cry

explanation.walkthrough: The Queen's Speech opens the UK Parliament; here the queen is a female cat.
explanation.definitionFit: The cry of a cat, the sound a queen cat makes.

clue.text: Bare all in review as dancer

indicators.note: a review looks over and reworks, so the letters of bare all in are reordered

explanation.surface: A dancer strips off in a stage revue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'review' plays on revue, a stage show.
explanation.definitionFit: A ballerina is a female ballet dancer.

clue.text: It reduces the noise when listeners get round piano

indicators.note: get round means the two words for listeners surround the letter for piano

parts.note: an ear is a listener
lug is slang for ear, another listener
P is the musical abbreviation for piano, softly

explanation.surface: A device to dull sound for those near a piano.
explanation.definitionFit: A plug for the ear blocks sound to protect hearing.

clue.text: Old snare with points set up in grass

indicators.note: set up in a down clue means the run of letters is read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: a trap is a snare
S and E are compass points

explanation.surface: An ancient trap with spikes hidden in grass.
explanation.walkthrough: 'set up' turns OTRAPSE round to give the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Esparto is a tough Spanish grass used for paper and rope.

clue.text: Steps taken by sailor meeting mother and son on return

indicators.note: on return means the whole run of sailor, mother and son is read backwards

parts.note: AB is an able seaman, a sailor
MA is mother

explanation.surface: A sailor comes home and does a dance with his mother and son.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on return' turns ABMAS round to give the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: The samba is a Brazilian dance, and a dance is a set of steps.

clue.text: Lots of water going over vessel

indicators.note: going over means the word for lots of water flips backwards

parts.note: pools are bodies of water

explanation.surface: Waves wash over a boat.
explanation.definitionFit: A sloop is a one-masted sailing boat.

clue.text: Stays to raise point about speaker

indicators.note: about means the turned word goes round the speaker
to raise in a down clue means the word for point is turned upwards, read backwards

parts.note: to aim is to point
an orator is a public speaker

explanation.surface: Keeping one's position to make a point about a lecturer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stays' looks like a verb but is the plural noun; in a down clue 'to raise' reads upward, and 'about' wraps the turned word round the speaker.
explanation.definitionFit: Moratoria are suspensions or delays, stays of action, plural of moratorium.

clue.text: A king, infuriated, assembled a fleet

parts.note: R is rex, king
mad means angry

explanation.surface: An angry monarch gathered his ships.
explanation.definitionFit: An armada is a large fleet of warships, as the Spanish one of 1588.

clue.text: Gem that's right in ring

indicators.note: in means the letter for right is placed inside the word for ring

parts.note: a peal is a ringing of bells

explanation.surface: A jewel set correctly in a ring.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ring' looks like jewellery but is the sound of bells, PEAL.
explanation.definitionFit: A pearl is a precious lustrous bead used as a gem.

clue.text: Remove bugs from material girl runs around

parts.note: rep is a ribbed fabric, a material

indicators.note: around means the girl's name and the runs letter are turned backwards

parts.note: Margo is a girl's name
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: A girl in fabric scurrying about clearing pests.
explanation.walkthrough: 'around' turns MARGOR round into ROGRAM, which follows REP.
explanation.definitionFit: Debugging software means changing its code, rewriting the instructions a computer follows.

clue.text: Untreated wood is not a good bargain

parts.note: raw means untreated or unprocessed
deal is pine or fir timber

explanation.surface: Unseasoned timber is poor value.
explanation.definitionFit: A raw deal is unfair treatment, a poor exchange in which one side loses out.

clue.text: It's said to be planted amongst long grass

indicators.note: amongst means the word for planted sits inside the word for long grass

parts.note: a reed is a tall grass of wet places
put means placed or planted

explanation.surface: Something is rumoured to have been placed in the tall grass.
explanation.definitionFit: Reputed means generally believed or supposed, according to common report.

clue.text: Don't be offended — advice to breakfasting curate?

definitions.meaning: to accept a remark without resentment, an imperative here
the curate's egg was good in parts, so he should eat the good bits

explanation.walkthrough: The curate's egg comes from a Punch cartoon in which a curate, served a bad egg by his bishop, says parts of it are excellent.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to accept criticism graciously without resentment.

clue.text: Nursery cat said to be on track of bird

indicators.note: said means the pet name for a cat is spoken, not spelled

parts.note: kitty is a childish name for a cat
a wake is the track left by a ship

explanation.surface: A nursery's cat is reportedly hunting a bird.
explanation.definitionFit: The kittiwake is a small gull named for its call.

clue.text: Revolutionary means of measuring progress

parts.note: a gadget measuring how far a walker goes, counting steps, not a radical political yardstick

explanation.definitionFit: A pedometer counts steps to measure distance walked.

clue.text: Payment for accommodation can be a concern

definitions.meaning: money paid for a loan, accommodation in the banking sense
a stake or share in a business

explanation.definitionFit: Interest is a charge for borrowed money and also a share or stake in something.

clue.text: Recklessly staged grand war in this state?

indicators.note: recklessly means the three words staged, grand and war are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: A grand war mounted carelessly leads to bitter hostility.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes two parties in open hostility, ready to fight.

clue.text: Prize American fish to catch

parts.note: the gar is a North American freshwater fish
to land is to catch a fish

explanation.surface: A trophy for landing a fish in the States.
explanation.definitionFit: A garland is a wreath awarded as an honour or prize.

clue.text: Severe reprimands for space travellers

definitions.meaning: sharp tellings-off, as in getting a rocket

explanation.definitionFit: A rocket is British slang for a harsh telling-off, and also a craft that flies into space.

clue.text: Service provided in mountainous area

parts.note: Mass is a church service
if means provided that

explanation.surface: A church service held in the mountains.
explanation.definitionFit: A massif is a compact group of mountains.

clue.text: Person flying from Alberta, via Toronto

indicators.note: from means the letters are taken out of the run of words Alberta, via Toronto

explanation.surface: A traveller on a flight between two Canadian cities.
explanation.definitionFit: An aviator is a pilot, someone who flies an aircraft.

clue.text: Time to study in part of the flight

parts.note: to read is to study, as at university

explanation.surface: Taking time to read on an aeroplane.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flight' suggests air travel but means a flight of stairs.
explanation.definitionFit: A tread is the flat part of a stair one steps on.

clue.text: Match points are given after short contest

annotationWithheld.why: Match points are given after short contest: COMP (short contest) + ARE gives the answer, but 'points' has no job; no parse found and no blog located
annotationWithheld.clue: Match points are given after short contest

clue.text: Change produced by later reform

indicators.note: reform means the letters of later are formed again in a new order

explanation.surface: Change will come from a future reform.
explanation.definitionFit: To alter is to modify or make different.

clue.text: Sour ship's officer producing impasse on board

parts.note: stale means gone off or sour
a mate is a ship's officer below the captain

explanation.surface: A grumpy officer brings a ship's affairs to a deadlock.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on board' sounds nautical but means a chessboard.
explanation.definitionFit: Stalemate is the chess position where the player to move has no legal move, so a draw.

clue.text: The name is right

definitions.meaning: what a book, film or song is called
a legal entitlement or claim, as to property

explanation.definitionFit: A title is what a work is called, and also a legal claim of ownership.

clue.text: Addict's run to earth after taking ecstasy

definitions.note: read as addict is, the 's being a contraction

indicators.note: after taking means the word for run to earth holds the drug's letter inside it

parts.note: to run to earth is to find after a search
E is the drug ecstasy

explanation.surface: A drug user is tracked down after taking pills.
explanation.definitionFit: A fiend is an enthusiast or user hooked on something, as in a dope fiend.

clue.text: Soldier roughly arrested, brought before court finally

indicators.note: roughly means the letters of arrested are rearranged loosely
finally means only the last letter of court is used

explanation.surface: A soldier is manhandled under arrest and taken to court.
explanation.walkthrough: 'roughly' shuffles the eight letters of arrested; 'brought before' puts them ahead of the final letter of court.
explanation.definitionFit: Desert Rats was the nickname of the British 7th Armoured Division in North Africa, so one of its soldiers.
